transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this pre-air lock meeting started. We've got the finale going live Saturday at 9 PM Eastern, and I need to finalize the voting package today so we can document everything before transmission. We've got standards, platform production, rights, and data protection all in the room. Let's walk through the current draft — viewers can vote by SMS or through an online portal, and voting is open to our broadcast audience. Before I make the binding call on the final package, I want to hear from each of you on your areas. Who wants to start?

transcript.text: I'll start, Mara. I'd like to walk the room through what the memo specifies before you make your binding call, so we can make sure the final package is fully compliant. Let me share those details now.

I completed our platform certification test this morning, and the results are split: the SMS integration failed certification, while the web portal passed. So as it stands right now, we cannot offer SMS voting on Saturday — only the online portal is certified. Additionally, the approved web portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted, which the current draft doesn't mention. We'll need to update the voting package to reflect both of these realities before Mara makes her binding call.

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue with the voting interface. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today, and here's what it covers: the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The problem is that the current draft interface still contains performance clips. So before we finalize this package, those performance clips need to be removed from the voting interface — only names and approved headshots are cleared.

transcript.text: I need to flag a data protection issue with the current draft. I completed my privacy review with the voting vendor this week, and it establishes two requirements that the draft does not yet reflect. First, participation must be limited to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada — but the draft still describes worldwide participation. Second, voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days, and the draft currently has no deletion step at all. Both of these need to be incorporated into the final voting package before Mara makes her binding call.

transcript.text: Here are the specifics from the current standards memo, which was issued after the draft voting rules were circulated. The memo establishes three requirements: First, voters must be at least 13 years old. Second, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account. Third, voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. None of these are reflected in the current draft, so all three need to be incorporated into the final voting package before you make your binding call, Mara.
